title: Open model admission playbook and pinning guidance for experimental variants
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: Provide a prescriptive, operational playbook for admitting new open models (community weights and experimental variants) into the Redwood model catalog. This ticket clarifies requirements for when to pin a variant, how to record compatibility notes, and what automated checks gate admission and rollouts.

Problem statement: The current intake process is inconsistent across reviewers: some models are fully pinned on intake, others are released unpinned and later cause runtime regressions or unexpected cost/latency spikes. We need a deterministic decision path plus automation that reduces reviewer judgment calls and shortens time-to-safe-availability for high-value community models.

Goals:
- Define a decision graph that maps model signals to admission outcomes (pinned / soft-pinned / unpinned + canary).
- Specify the runtime and validation probes required for each admission outcome (kernel compatibility, quantization test, perf profile).
- Enumerate required catalog metadata fields and compatibility-note templates that are machine-readable where possible.
- Provide acceptance criteria and rollout/rollback guidance developers and catalog reviewers can follow.

Stakeholders: PM (owner), Runtime/Serving eng, Model-onboarding squad, Console UX, Security (for KMS/audit concerns), Solutions (customer-facing risk comms).
acceptance_criteria: Decision graph documented: a single-page flow that maps intake signals (model arch, weight provenance, provided tokenizers, quantization path, kernel profile) to one of three outputs: Pin, Soft-Pin (canary with constraints), Unpinned with advisory; reviewers can follow it without additional clarifications.

Automated intake checks implemented in the ingestion pipeline: basic file validation, format detection, a lightweight runtime probe that runs on a small test sequence and returns kernel compatibility, peak memory estimate, and 95th percentile token latency for a standard prompt.
Pin metadata fields added to catalog schema: 'pin_state' (pinned|soft-pinned|unpinned), 'pin_reason' (freeform), 'compat_signals' (list), 'runtime_profile_link' (URL).
Console UI changes: catalog listings show pin_state badge and a short compatibility excerpt; reviewers can attach a runtime profile link and rollback sentinel from the model detail page.

Rollout playbooks: for soft-pinned models, a canary template exists that enforces route caps, latency SLO gates, and automatic fallback to a pinned model variant on error or quality regression detected by an eval set.

Runtime safety gate: admission pipeline blocks 'unpinned' or 'soft-pinned' release if kernel incompatibility prevents quantized execution on standard GPU families used by Dedicated and Hosted (NVidia A100, H100), unless override justification provided and security reviewed.
Docs: One PRD and a reviewer checklist live in Confluence/Docs for catalog admins and a short FAQ for customers about what 'soft-pinned' means for model stability and cost.
E2E test: a CI job exercises the intake path for at least two sample community models to validate the decision graph and automated checks (green in CI before release of playbook).
out_of_scope: Full retraining or model quality improvements — this ticket is about onboarding and serving assumptions only.
Major UI redesign of the Console beyond pin_state badges and links.
Changes to pricing or billing model for community weights (handled by Pricing team).
proposed_solution: Author a compact decision graph (SVG + markdown) that reviewers can follow — embed in Confluence and link from the intake UI.
Enhance the ingestion pipeline to run a lightweight runtime probe that returns a small JSON summary (kernel hints, memory footprint, perf sample) and surface those signals as 'compat_signals'.
Define catalog schema additions and enforce them at intake time; default pin_state is 'unpinned' unless probe or provenance indicates instability or broken kernel paths.

Introduce 'soft-pinned' with strict canary template: max 5% of traffic, token caps, automated perf/quality monitors tied to the eval set; automatic demote to 'unpinned' and traffic reroute on breach of SLOs or eval regressions.
Create reviewer checklist and required justification fields for manual overrides (free-text 'pin_reason' plus link to security review or runtime ticket if applicable).
Instrument the Console to show pin_state and runtime_profile_link; add audit log entries for pin/unpin actions (who, when, reason).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-pinning community models slows availability and reduces model discovery. Mitigation: Use conservative criteria for 'Pin' and prefer 'soft-pinned' for most experimental variants with tight canary constraints.
Risk: Automated probes may yield false negatives for exotic hardware. Mitigation: Flag 'unknown-hardware' compat_signals and require human reviewer for such cases; log samples for later analysis.
Risk: Customers misinterpret 'soft-pinned' as production-grade. Mitigation: Clear UX language, FAQ, and EVAL-linked quality notes visible on model detail pages.
Risk: Automation pipeline increases CI time. Mitigation: Probe runs are lightweight and sampled; only one probe per model per architecture family on intake, cached for subsequent runs.
followups: ENG: implement intake probe service and return compat_signals (ENG-22712) — owner: Runtime team.
Console: add pin_state badge and runtime_profile_link to model detail page — owner: Console UX.
Security: review override flow and audit log requirements and sign off — owner: Security.
PM: publish the playbook, host a reviewer training session, and collect feedback after two weeks of use.
